reading.body:
Digital Realty's DFW16 facility in Richardson totals 106,500 square feet with 2N cooling redundancy, meaning it can sustain full load with any single cooling unit down. The operator publishes no megawatt capacity figure for this building, so its power draw relative to other Texas data centers cannot be read directly from the spec sheet.

Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities, but only 18 publish power capacity figures totaling 468 MW. This facility ranks 19th among published Texas capacities, placing it below the threshold of disclosed power but within a campus that Digital Realty names with reference to the Dallas-Fort Worth region, where the operator maps at least four distinct buildings on separate Richardson addresses.

Without published megawatts, this facility's relevance to AI scaling cannot be assessed from the data provided. The 2N cooling standard qualifies it for enterprise workloads including high-density compute, but whether the building is leased, to whom, and what density it currently runs are not published. The campus itself remains largely opaque to capacity tracking in a state where most facilities do not disclose power.
